name: Murgh Musallam
ingredients: Saffron strands soaked in warm milk
Whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves)
instructions: 1. Marinate the whole chicken with ginger-garlic paste, yogurt, and powdered spices, allowing it to rest for at least 4 hours.
2. Prepare a stuffing of boiled eggs and nuts mixed with some masala.
3. Stuff the chicken cavity and truss it securely with kitchen twine.
4. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and sear the chicken on all sides until golden brown.
5. Remove the chicken, then prepare the gravy using fried onions, nut paste, whole spices, and the remaining marinade.
6. Place the chicken back in the pot, cover, and cook on low heat (dum style) until tender, basting occasionally.
7. Garnish with saffron milk and fresh coriander before serving.
description: Originating from the royal kitchens of the Mughals and perfected in the Awadh region of Uttar Pradesh, Murgh Musallam is a festive, celebratory dish representing the opulence of Indian culinary history. 'Musallam' means 'whole' or 'intact', signifying the grand presentation of the dish as a centerpiece for royal banquets.
